newsitem.title: USA: Clinton notifies Congress on Sierre Leone action.
newsitem.headline: Clinton notifies Congress on Sierre Leone action.

text.p: President Bill Clinton informed Congress on Monday he had ordered U.S. military forces to evacuate Americans from Sierre Leone "due to the uncertain security situation" in the African state.

In a five paragraph letter to House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich and Sen. Strom Thurmond, dean of the Senate, Clinton said there was no evidence U.S. citizens were being targeted but that violence in the capital, Freetown, subjected them to continued risks.

"On May 29 and May 30, due to the uncertain security situation and the possible threat to American citizens and the American Embassy in Sierre Leone, approximately 200 U.S. military personnel, including an 11-member Special Forces detachment, were positioned in Freetown to prepare for the evacuation," he said.

Clinton said a pullout of Americans and designated third country citizens began on May 30, after 18 Americans had departed the previous day on a chartered British flight. "Although U.S. forces are equipped for combat, the evacuation has been undertaken solely for the purpose of protecting American citizens and property," he said.
He added that U.S. forces would leave Sierre Leone "as soon as evacuation operations are complete and enhanced security and locations in and around Freetown is no longer required."

"I am providing this report as part of my efforts to keep Congress fully informed, consistent with the War Powers Resolution," Clinton wrote, referring to a Vietnam era law that gives Congress the final say in sending troops to combat.

Neither Clinton nor any of his presidential predecessors has recognised the War Powers Resolution, arguing that it is an unconstitutional usurpation of the chief executive's power to conduct foreign policy. But every recent president has complied with notification requirements of the law whenever U.S. forces have been put at risk to avoid confrontation with the legislative branch of the government.
